chunks: And from him, from 'Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the As-Sa'ibah, so he said: 'Look in the Quran for what contains the phrase 'freeing a slave'; that, O 'Ammar is the Sa'ibah upon whom there is no guardianship for any of the people except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
And whose guardianship belongs to Allah, it belongs to the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).

And whose guardianship belongs to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then indeed his guardianship belongs to the Imam (peace be upon him), and his blood-money is upon the Imam, and his inheritance is for him.'

key_terms.السَّائِبَة: A type of freed slave whose guardianship is assigned to a specific entity

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Sa'ibah and who inherits the freed slave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a theological hierarchy of guardianship (wilayah) by linking the status of the 'Sa'ibah' to the Quranic phrase 'freeing a slave' (4:92). He elucidates that this freed slave’s allegiance ultimately rests with the Imam, who assumes his blood-money (diyah) and inheritance, thereby grounding the Imam’s authority in scriptural precedent and establishing a direct spiritual and legal lineage from Allah to the Prophet and then to the Imam.
